title: Ice Cream 1.5L

drivers.name: Price increase (2.3%)
drivers.evidence: At $6.56, recent median is 38.5 (12.5% below baseline). 2026-09-28 (same price) sold 24 units (x0.54). No promotions at this price. Noise-adjusted price effect suggests ~12.5% drop.

drivers.name: Supplier delivery short
drivers.evidence: Planner note indicates supply risk. Could lead to stockouts, reducing sales. Moderate downside impact. No historical data on delivery short, so conservative shrink.

adjustment.analysis: Baseline median is 44.1. No events or promotions in target week. Price increased 2.3% to $6.56, which is above regular. Recent weeks at $6.56 show median 38.5 (vs baseline 44.1), a 12.5% drop. This aligns with past price sensitivity: no promotions seen at this price, but 2026-09-28 (same price) sold 24 units (x0.54 vs baseline). The noise-adjusted price effect is conservative. Supplier delivery short warning adds supply risk—downside. No evidence of promotion lift. Classical model suggests 1.00, but judgment overrides: price increase likely suppresses demand. Shrink effect toward 1.0 due to limited data at this price point.

brief:
PRODUCT: Ice Cream 1.5L | category Frozen | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-30 to 2026-12-06 (8 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 6.56 (+2.3% vs regular price 6.41)
  planner notes: Supplier warns of a short delivery

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 44.1 | 5%-95%: 10.5 - 75.8 | 10%-90%: 19.4 - 71.2

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-36% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
